title: Carrollton halls and social clubs
summary: They discuss St. Dominic Hall, Eagle Hall, and the social aid clubs that still parade.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Was there much going on up in Carleton? Any dance halls or clubs? What kind of, where did they have music up there? Well, they had St. Dominic Hall
and Lincoln Park, that was out there. That was in Carleton, wasn't it?
Remember St. Dominic Hall where it was? That was out there by the public Belt Railroad. Near the river?
Yes, near the river, right by St. Dominic
School, Church. Oh, I guess it's still there then. Yes, sir. Somebody told me there was an Eagle Hall out there. Do you remember any Eagle Hall? The Eagle Hall was up

near Protection Levy. Is that still in Carleton? Yes, sir. That was still in Carleton. That was about a block from Protection Levy. Protection Levy, right on the other side of Protection there was Jefferson Tarish. Oh, yes.
Today, there's one club up there that still puts on parades called the Merry-Go-Round Club. That may be a more modern club than the days you were there, I guess.
Yes, they had all those Merry-Go-Rounds and different things, too. And the Carlton Club, Jefferson City, Buzzards. Oh, yes. That's out towards the Irish Channel. Yes, that's down
A little below Peters Avenue. They still give parades every carnival. Yeah, every carnival. They walk you all over the Orleans.
